text:
sasha: Heads-up — seeing repeated latency spikes from rack-r3 (03:14 UTC). Multiple tenants' workloads hitting high interconnect fanout; NVLink dport queues trending up. Anyone on-call for that rack?

infra-bot: Alert: rack-r3 aggregate-port-5 throughput 98% for 7m; nvlink_errs=12; pcie_retransmits rising

mika: saw the alert, digging into PCIe stats. retransmits up, top-of-rack tx queues climbing. metric snippet: `tc -s qdisc show dev to-rack-agg` shows backlog

jamie: could be noisy neighbor. which tenants are spiking?

ash: top offenders: t-omega (latency-sensitive training), t-lilac (batch infer), t-hawthorn (mixed). t-omega is on a shared slice and is dominating fabric via cross-host kv fetches. I moved t-omega to a dedicated pool and applied a temporary egress cap.

ash: command: `redwoodctl tenant update t-omega --egress-limit 100mbps --preferred-pool dedicated-pool-d2`

mika: nice. also enabling kvcache warmup on r3 to reduce cross-host fetch pressure. will watch queue drain.

jamie: can we add a soft-quarantine QoS for heavy tails so we don't cause cross-host storms? a transient tag before preemption would help.

sasha: yes — avoid mass preemption (last time it caused a cascade). propose a routing policy: prefer dedicated when rack-egress>80% for 10m, and mark offending tenant with soft-quarantine for 15m.

ash: applying a canary policy now: `policies set routing rack-r3 prefer=dedicated when egress>80% duration=10m` and `tenants tag t-omega add soft-quarantine ttl=15m`

infra-bot: Incident created: #INC-117 — rack-r3 interconnect fanout & tenant noisy neighbor. Notifying ops and eng-infra.

mika: monitoring graphs show egress drop from 98% -> 45% after the move; nvlink errs falling. will keep for 30m then recommend next steps.

sasha: thanks everyone. follow-up items: (1) evaluate slice fractioning for noisy tenants, (2) investigate hardware margin on agg-port-5, (3) add a regression alert for cross-host kv fetch rate. I'll add to the eng-infra weekly agenda. :thumbsup:
